question: On 15 July 2025, the European Union and Iceland signed a memorandum of understanding in the area of fisheries and maritime affairs, making reference to the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework1. Meanwhile, a bill that would permanently ban commercial whaling is expected to be discussed in Iceland in February 20272.

Yet, in February 2026, the European Investment Bank (EIB) granted a EUR 100 million loan to Arion Bank to support the sustainable blue economy in Iceland, Greenland and the Faroe Islands3. Hvalur hf., the last Icelandic commercial whaling company, which caught 93 fin whales out of a quota of 150 in 20264, holds a stake of approximately 2.66 % in the bank5.
Its financial investments help maintain its profitability despite the decline in its whaling activity. In view of the above: 1.
Can the Commission ask the EIB for details of the safeguards preventing this loan from indirectly benefiting whale companies?
Will it organise a public hearing on EU funding for maritime activities in third countries?
Will it give priority to European fishing communities and exclude companies directly involved in commercial whaling from receiving funding?
